name: Repainting vs Full Interior Paint Restoration in Older Los Angeles Homes

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between repainting and full interior paint restoration for older Los Angeles homes, and when is restoration worth the extra cost?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between repainting and full interior paint restoration for older Los Angeles homes, and when is restoration worth the extra cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: In older Los Angeles homes—Craftsman, Spanish, Mid-Century, or Victorians—there is a meaningful difference between a simple repaint and full interior paint restoration. A repaint typically includes cleaning, filling small holes, caulking gaps, light sanding, and applying new primer and paint. It is primarily cosmetic and works well for newer construction or surfaces in decent condition. Full restoration goes deeper. It may involve stabilizing loose plaster, stitching recurring cracks, addressing chronic movement joints, dealing with multiple failing paint layers, and using specialized primers or skim coats to create a uniform surface. On homes with potential lead paint, restoration should use dust-minimizing and lead-safe methods and potentially stripping unstable layers. Restoration contractors may also match historical color palettes, sheens, and textures to preserve architectural character. This level of work costs more upfront but is worth it when walls and ceilings have extensive alligatoring, flaking, recurrent cracks, or when a home’s historic aesthetic is a priority. It reduces the risk that new paint will quickly fail, giving you a more durable and authentic finish. Discuss your goals, budget, and how long you plan to stay in the home to decide which approach makes more sense.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repainting usually means basic prep and new color, while full interior paint restoration on older Los Angeles homes involves more extensive repairs: crack stitching, plaster stabilization, lead-safe practices, and historically appropriate finishes. Restoration is worth it when you want to preserve original character and prevent ongoing failures rather than just cover defects.
